Subject: Audit log export — sliced delivery, checksums, and erase verification

Hi Aditya,

Thanks again for taking time to speak with our security team last week. A few follow-ups from legal/compliance:

1) For tenant-level audit/access log exports, can you confirm the delivery options (single archive vs sliced batches per day/hour)? We need recommended approaches for 1+TB exports.

2) For each exported slice, what metadata is included in the manifest? Specifically: time window, source cluster id, schema version, event count, and a cryptographic checksum. Will Redwood provide SHA256 checksums for each slice?

3) If we request retention deletion/proof of erase later, what evidence can Redwood supply to show slices were removed (manifest tombstone, signed delete event, certificate)? Our auditors ask for auditable proof of deletion tied to tenant id and export id.

4) Are exported artifacts encrypted at rest in transit and is there a KMS trace we can attach to the manifest for key identifiers?

If you can send a short written Q&A we can share with our auditors. If better, we can schedule a short call.

Thanks,

Maria Lopez
Security & Privacy Lead
FreshHealth, Inc.

Subject: Re: Audit log export — sliced delivery, checksums, and erase verification

Hi Maria — thanks for the clear list. High level answers below; I put Tessa and Grace on to add detail and attach the PDF that outlines our standard export options.

1) Delivery: we support both single-archive (Zip/Parquet bundle) and time-sliced deliveries. For >1TB we recommend day-level slices by default (configurable to hourly for high-activity tenants). Sliced delivery improves resumability and parallel transfer.

2) Manifest metadata: each slice manifest includes slice_id, start/end ISO timestamps, cluster_id, model/runtime schema_version, record_count, byte_size, compression, filename, and SHA256 checksum. We also embed export_request_id and tenant_id.

3) Delete / proof: We generate a signed delete receipt (export_id + slice_id + timestamp + operator_id) when a retention deletion is executed. That receipt contains a signature from our KMS-backed signing key and can be cross-referenced to the original manifest. For higher assurance we can provide an export tombstone file and the audit event showing the delete action.

4) Encryption/KMS: exports are encrypted in transit (TLS) and at rest using envelope encryption. The manifest includes key_id (KMS ARN) used to wrap the slice key. We can include KMS key fingerprints in the manifest if needed.

I'll leave technical specifics and a sample manifest to Tessa (adds checksums sample) and Grace (operational SLAs and retention windows). Attached: audit_export_options.pdf (short summary of available export formats and recommended patterns).

Best,
Aditya Rao
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Attachment: audit_export_options.pdf (summary of formats and recommended slicing)

Hi Maria — attaching the two redacted examples you asked for and answers to the three bullets inline.

--- legal hold / manifest flagging ---
We support hold_status and hold_id fields in the slice manifest. When a legal hold is applied our deletion workflow marks the slice with hold_status=true and prevents the automated purge. The hold action itself generates an immutable hold_event that is recorded in our tenant audit trail (audit_event_type=legal_hold, actor, timestamp, hold_id).

--- chain of custody ---
We can emit a chain_of_custody.jsonl file as part of the handover. Each line is a signed entry: action (created|transferred|verified|deleted), actor_id, ISO timestamp, export_id, slice_id, signature. Signatures are HSM-backed and can be verified with our public certificate (will include cert fingerprint in the package). This is what auditors typically expect.

--- samples (attached) ---
Attachments in this message:
- manifest-sample.jsonl — one redacted slice manifest (fields: slice_id, tenant_id, start_ts, end_ts, cluster_id, schema_v, record_count, byte_size, filename, sha256, key_id, hold_status, hold_id)
- checksums-sha256.txt — simple two-line format mapping file names to SHA256 checksums (we include timestamp and export_id header)

Notes on verification: we recommend verifying the SHA256 against the downloaded slice before importing. We also include an optional signed manifest_summary.sig for high-assurance verifications. For very large exports we can provide a per-chunk Merkle proof on request (extra project work).

If it helps, I can schedule a 30-minute demo of an export handover run-through with our delivery engineer.

Regards,

Tessa Morgan
Product Security Lead | Redwood Inference
